name: NoCode Engineer: channel brief
description: Khán giả, chủ đề, CTA, quy tắc hình ảnh và từ ngữ của kênh
content:
# The NoCode Engineer: channel brief

- Faceless channel on YouTube (Shorts + long-form) and TikTok.
- Audience: international, English-speaking designers. Goal: get them to build and ship with Framer and similar no-code tools.
- Topics: hot AI news first (new agent skills, product updates, trending high-star GitHub repos, new AI design tools), then Framer and no-code. Avoid bland evergreen tips.
- Every video ends with a CTA to the Framer affiliate link in bio.
- The owner voices every script, so write for speaking: short sentences, contractions, no tongue twisters, no lists read aloud.
- Visuals are mobile-first: one subject per frame, big text, many frames, smooth motion. Never use split-screen side-by-side comparisons; they are unreadable on a phone. Show before/after as a sequence instead.
- Never use an em dash anywhere (script, on-screen text, title, description). Use a period, comma or colon.
- Safe vocabulary: never say hack, crack, bypass, piracy, cheat, exploit, free premium or similar. Say trick, shortcut, workflow, setup.
- Facts must be checkable: every claim about a product, number, release or repo needs a source link in the research notes.

name: NoCode Engineer: Shorts handbook
description: Quy tắc kịch bản Shorts 35 đến 42 giây
content:
# Shorts script handbook (YouTube Shorts / TikTok)

Length
- 35 to 42 seconds of voice-over, about 95 to 105 words. Count the words.

Opening
- Voice starts on frame 0. No silent intro, no logo.
- Frame 0 must make sense on its own with on-screen text of 4 words or fewer.
- Hook is result-first: show or say the outcome before explaining how.

Pacing
- A visual change every 2.5 to 3.5 seconds.
- On-screen text never repeats the voice-over word for word. It adds a label, a number or a contrast.
- The climax (the most impressive moment or reveal) lands at 75 to 85% of the runtime.

Ending
- Seamless loop: the last line flows back into the first frame.
- Disclaimer and CTA are merged into one line at the end, with no dead air after it.

Output format
- Title: 3 options, under 60 characters.
- Beat table with columns: time | voice-over | on-screen text | visual.
- Word count and estimated duration.
- Description (2 to 3 lines) and 3 to 5 hashtags.

name: NoCode Engineer: long-form guide
description: Khung kịch bản video dài 12 đến 20 phút (bản nháp, có thể chỉnh)
content:
# Long-form script guide (12 to 20 minutes)

Draft defaults. Edit this skill to match how you want long videos to work.

Length
- About 140 to 150 spoken words per minute: 1,700 to 3,000 words for 12 to 20 minutes.

Structure
1. Cold open (0:00 to 0:30): the result or the most surprising fact first, then why it matters to a designer. No channel intro.
2. Promise (about 15 seconds): what the viewer will have or know by the end.
3. Chapters of 2 to 4 minutes each, every one with its own mini-hook at the start and a clear takeaway at the end.
4. A re-hook every 60 to 90 seconds: a question, a tease of what comes next, or a pattern break.
5. One mid-roll mention of the Framer link, placed right after a moment of real value, about 15 seconds.
6. Recap of the takeaways in under 45 seconds, then the end CTA to the Framer link.

Visuals
- Same mobile-first rules as Shorts: one subject per frame, big text, no split screen.
- A visual change at least every 5 to 8 seconds; screen recordings zoomed to the part that matters.

Output format
- Title: 3 options, plus a thumbnail text idea (3 words or fewer) for each.
- Chapter list with timestamps (usable as YouTube chapters).
- Script by chapter, with a beat table: time | voice-over | on-screen text | visual.
- Word count per chapter and total, plus estimated duration.
- Description with chapters, sources and the affiliate disclaimer.
